title: Small molecule structure elucidation from NMR spectra with generative and reasoning models.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Elucidating the structures of unknown small molecules remains a major challenge in chemistry, pharmacology, and drug discovery. While nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is the gold standard for structure elucidation, interpreting spectra remains labor-intensive and requires expert knowledge to navigate the vast space of possible structures. Here, we present an AI system for rapid, automated de novo structure elucidation that combines a molecular generative model with a scientific reasoning agent. Its generative component, CHEFNMR2, is an atomic flow-matching model that predicts smal

bioTriage.summary: The authors present an AI system that combines a molecular generative model (CHEFNMR2, an atomic flow-matching model) with a scientific reasoning agent to automatically determine the structure of unknown small molecules from NMR spectra. This addresses the labor-intensive, expert-dependent bottleneck in NMR-based structure elucidation, which is central to chemistry, pharmacology, and drug discovery.

title: Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Disease-relevant changes in RNA processing frequently evade detection because they are missing from transcript annotations. Here, we introduce Torino , a computational framework that learns patterns of RNA processing directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data by modeling how coverage varies across samples, in datasets spanning tissues, individuals and disease states. Torino adapts non-negative matrix factorization to decompose coverage into patterns that capture RNA processing events, and to quantify their usage across samples, without transcript annotations. bioTriage.summary: The authors present Torino, a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. By adapting non-negative matrix factorization to model how read coverage varies across samples, Torino identifies unannotated RNA processing events and quantifies their usage across tissues, individuals, and disease states, revealing links between previously hidden processing patterns and disease risk.

title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),

bioTriage.summary: InterPro is a freely accessible database that integrates predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to classify protein sequences into families and predict domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, achieving extensive coverage of UniProtKB and linking to resources like Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central hub for protein functional annotation.

title: Gut‒liver‒brain axis signature of cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment is consistent across multi-national cohorts.
abstract: Cognitive impairment in cirrhosis is associated with an altered gut‒liver‒brain axis, but geographic variations in diet and clinical practices may limit generalizability. We investigated consistency of microbial signatures for cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment across four countries. We enrolled outpatients with cirrhosis from USA, Denmark, Lithuania, and Mexico who underwent Psychometric Hepatic Encephalopathy Score (PHES) testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy (CHE), and stool shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Taxonomic and functional associations with PHES were evaluated after adjustme

bioTriage.summary: This study examined whether gut microbiome signatures associated with cognitive impairment in cirrhosis are consistent across patients from four countries (USA, Denmark, Lithuania, Mexico). Using stool shotgun metagenomics and PHES testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy, the authors identified taxonomic and functional microbial associations with cognitive scores that held across diverse geographic cohorts despite differences in diet and clinical practice. The findings support a reproducible gut‒liver‒brain axis signature underlying cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment.

title: Single-cell analysis of chromatin state and transcriptome in the human basal ganglia.
abstract: The basal ganglia are central to motor control, learning, emotion, and reward processing, and their dysfunction contributes to many neurological and psychiatric disorders. Here, we generated a single-cell multi-omic atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight basal ganglia regions from neurotypical human donors. This atlas resolved cell-type- and region-specific landscapes of active and repressive candidate cis-regulatory elements and delineated gene regulatory networks underlying cell identity. We found that the combinatorial expression of homeobox transcription factors pro

bioTriage.summary: This study presents a single-cell multi-omic atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight human basal ganglia regions, revealing cell-type- and region-specific regulatory landscapes and gene regulatory networks. The authors identify combinatorial homeobox transcription factor expression as a key driver of cell identity in this brain region. This resource provides a foundation for understanding basal ganglia function and dysfunction in neurological and psychiatric disorders.

title: A droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing method for the high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within individual cells.
abstract: Recently, long-read sequencing methods have revolutionized genomic research by allowing the resolution of previously inaccessible regions across the genome. However, the throughput and scalability of these methods have hindered their general application in the field. To address this limitation, we developed droplet-based methods for the single-cell profiling of chromatin accessibility (droplet-based single-cell Nanopore ATAC-seq, dscNanoATAC) and histone modifications (droplet-based single-cell NanoCUT&Tag, dscNanoCUT) by combining a commercial microfluidic device and long-read sequencing plat

bioTriage.summary: The authors developed droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing methods, dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT, by combining a commercial microfluidic device with nanopore sequencing to profile chromatin accessibility and histone modifications in individual cells at high throughput. This addresses previous scalability limitations of long-read single-cell epigenomics, enabling multidimensional regulatory element profiling within single cells.

title: Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody-antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity.
abstract: Co-folding models are increasingly used to predict antibody-antigen complexes for epitope mapping, candidate triage and structure-guided de novo design or engineering, yet the latest generation of these models has not been compared under standardized conditions. We benchmark AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast and OpenDDE on 200 test-set complexes (121 Fvs and 79 VHHs) from SAbDab2-Bench, a newly curated dataset, and a reconstructed antibody-antigen subset of FoldBench, Ab-FoldBench. Using standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics that isolate the antibody-antigen inte

bioTriage.summary: This paper benchmarks five open-source co-folding models (AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast, and OpenDDE) on antibody-antigen complex prediction using a newly curated dataset of 200 complexes (SAbDab2-Bench) plus a reconstructed FoldBench antibody subset. It evaluates docking accuracy and interaction specificity under standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics, providing a fair comparison of the latest generation of co-folding tools for antibody-antigen modeling.

title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of ge

bioTriage.summary: PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges in data integration: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.
